newsitem.title: USA: Big Rivers files Chapter 11 to ease partnership.
newsitem.headline: Big Rivers files Chapter 11 to ease partnership.

text.p: Big Rivers Electric Corp said on Wednesday that it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as a means to ease its partnership with PacificCorp.

PacifiCorp, which issued a separate statement supporting the bankruptcy filing, plans to operate Big Rivers's generating facilities during the next 25 years, while selling power to Big Rivers and marketing the surplus.
Under Chapter 11, Big Rivers is authorized to operate in the ordinary course of business and it filed a motion seeking approval to assure that business continues.

Big Rivers, an electricity cooperative in western Kentucky with 91,000 customers, filed the prepackaged bankruptcy mainly because it expected decreased cash flow, because the rates for two aluminum smelters are projected to decrease at the end of the year, said Jimmy Jones, vice general manager of public relations.
Big Rivers projected a default on its debt due to the rate decline for NS Inc and Alcan Aluminum Ltd, which consume the bulk of the cooperative's power, Jones said.
The smelter operators agreed to support the PacifiCorp deal and they have put hold on litigation against Big Rivers.
Jones said the bankruptcy will result in lower rates, because Big Rivers would restructure its debt with the Rural Utility Service, a federal agency, and receive lease payments from PacifiCorp.
Big Rivers will conduct transmission services for its four distribution cooperatives, it said.
Litigation with the smelters started after the cooperative completed a 420 megawatt coal-fired plant in the mid-1980s. The plant was started in the 1970s, when oil prices were high, Jones said.
Upon completion, Big River had a plant generating power it could not sell at a profitable price and $1 billion in debt, Jones said.
Jones said he is "confident that the reorganization will leave Big Rivers a financially viable entity."
